h1: The 8 Best Toaster Ovens for One Person of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Toaster Ovens for One Person: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 compact toaster ovens for one person scored on capacity, controls and footprint, from the Dash Mini to Breville Smart Ovens.
summary: The Breville BOV450XL Mini Smart Oven is the one to buy if you cook for yourself most nights: sized for a single portion with smarter heating than budget ovens. The Breville BOV680BSS adds air frying and a Crispy Reheat mode that suits leftovers. On a tight budget, the Dash Mini or the Elite Gourmet ETO236 cover toast and reheating. Pick the Elite Gourmet ETO449X for the best simple dial oven with real meal capacity.
intro: A one-person kitchen has different needs from a family one. You rarely need to cook for four, but you do reheat leftovers, crisp a slice of pizza, toast bread and bake a single chicken thigh. A full-size toaster oven wastes counter space and takes longer to preheat for a meal that fits in a small tray.

We ranked eight compact ovens on how well they suit a solo cook. That meant real interior capacity, whether the controls are quick to use, how heat is delivered to a small load, and how much counter they claim. Scores lean on spec sheets and shopper reports rather than kitchen trials.

products.name: Breville BOV450XL Mini Smart Oven
products.verdict: Single-portion sizing with Breville's Element IQ heating, a clear step up from budget ovens.
products.description:
Breville's Mini Smart Oven is sized closer to solo cooking than the brand's larger models, and it uses Element IQ to adjust power delivery for a small load. Heating a single portion is exactly where cheap ovens waste energy and burn edges, and this one is built for it.

It costs more than the budget picks and the stainless body is not the smallest on the list, but the build quality shows. Against the BOV650XL it is slightly smaller and simpler, which suits a single person better. Check the listing for the exact accessories included.

Buy it if you cook at home most days and want the best everyday oven for one.
products.idealFor: People who cook at home most days and want one reliable oven.
products.skipIf: You only toast bread and want to spend as little as possible.

products.name: Breville BOV680BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Compact
products.verdict: A compact air fryer oven with a single-dial interface and a Crispy Reheat mode for leftovers.
products.description:
The BOV680BSS is the compact air fry model in Breville's lineup, with one dial instead of a multi-step menu. That makes a quick solo meal fast to set up, and the Crispy Reheat mode is built to re-crisp a single leftover portion rather than steam it soft.

It is the most expensive pick here and a newer listing with less history behind it. Compared with the BOV450XL you gain air frying and the leftover mode, but you pay a premium for them. If you rarely air fry, the cheaper Breville gives most of the value.

Best for someone who wants one appliance to replace an air fryer, a toaster and a microwave for reheating.
pros: Air fry in a compact body
Single dial is quick to use
products.idealFor: Solo cooks who want air frying and leftover crisping in one box.
products.skipIf: You never air fry and want the cheapest capable oven.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO449X Toaster Oven
products.verdict: 800W, 8.99L, dual analog dials. Compact yet big enough for a real single meal.
products.description:
The ETO449X uses two quartz elements and an 800W output in an 8.99L cavity, with a pizza function and plain analog dials rather than a digital menu. It reaches temperature quickly and there is nothing to learn.

It ranks below the Breville ovens because it has no smart power delivery and a less proven brand record, but it costs less. Next to the Elite Gourmet ETO490 it is the more compact choice, and the 8.99L interior still fits a small meal instead of just a slice of toast.

A good fit for a one-person kitchen that wants fast heating and simple controls.
products.idealFor: Solo cooks who want fast, no-fuss dials at a modest price.
products.skipIf: You want smart heating or air frying.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 2-in-1 Countertop Toaster Oven and Long Slot 2 Slice Toaster
products.verdict: A toaster and a 16.5L oven in one unit, saving a whole appliance's worth of counter.
products.description:
Hamilton Beach combines a 2-slice toaster and a 16.5L toaster oven in one stainless body. For a single person in a small kitchen, that means one appliance on the counter and not two, and the toast runs about 40 percent faster than a standard toaster according to the maker.

It costs more than the basic ovens and the larger body is not the most compact on the list. Compared with the Breville Mini, it lacks smart heating but adds a dedicated toaster, which matters if you toast bread every morning.

Pick it if breakfast toast is a daily habit and you want to free counter space.
products.idealFor: Daily toast eaters in small kitchens with little counter space.
products.skipIf: You want the smallest oven possible.

products.name: Breville BOV650XL Compact Smart Oven
products.verdict: 1800W fast preheat, still compact enough for one person.
products.description:
The BOV650XL is a small step up in size from the Mini and rated at 1800W for quick preheating. Expect room for one small pizza or a roast sized for a single plate, in a stainless body.

The jump from the BOV450XL is modest in price but also in what it adds for a single person. It ranks lower because the extra size is wasted when you only cook one portion, and the bigger footprint matters on a small counter. Check the listing for what is included.

Best for a solo cook who occasionally cooks for a guest and wants more room than the Mini.
products.idealFor: Solo cooks who sometimes host one guest.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO236 Compact 2-Slice Toaster Oven
products.verdict: The smallest oven here, with a built-in thermostat and a 15-minute timer.
products.description:
The ETO236 is a 2-slice compact oven with a built-in thermostat and a 15-minute timer. It is the easiest of the group to tuck into a studio kitchen, and the size matches single-portion everyday needs.

The small cavity and short timer limit what you can cook. It handles toast and a reheated slice well, but not a proper bake, which is where the larger Elite Gourmet ETO449X pulls ahead. It is a newer listing with less history behind it.

Good for toast, melts and quick reheating in the smallest possible footprint.
products.idealFor: Studio kitchens that need toast and reheating only.
products.skipIf: You want to bake or roast.

products.name: Dash Mini Toaster Oven
products.verdict: The least expensive oven here, with auto shutoff and a pizza function.
products.description:
The Dash Mini is the cheapest pick in the group and sized close to what one person cooks in one sitting. Auto shutoff with an indicator light keeps a solo reheat routine simple.

It is not sized for full meals, only snacks, and it has a shorter track record than the better-known ovens. It ranks below the ETO236 because that one adds a built-in thermostat, but it beats nothing on price.

Best for a dorm, a desk kitchen or a first apartment where you need a cheap way to reheat and toast.
products.idealFor: Dorms and first apartments on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want to cook full meals.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO490 9L/4-Slice Oven
products.verdict: A 9L, 4-slice oven with a 30-minute timer that covers real baking.
products.description:
The ETO490 offers a 9L cavity, a built-in thermostat and a 30-minute timer, enough for baking and roasting rather than just toast. That makes it useful for reheating meal-prep leftovers in one batch.

It is larger than the other budget ovens, so it ranks last for a one-person kitchen where space matters most. The ETO449X offers similar capacity in a quicker-heating package. A shorter track record also holds it back.

Worth it if you meal prep on weekends and need room for several portions at once.
products.idealFor: Weekend meal preppers reheating several portions.
products.skipIf: Counter space is your main limit.

whatMatters.factor: Match capacity to your actual meals
whatMatters.detail: Slice count is a rough guide, but what counts is whether your usual dish fits. A 2-slice oven handles toast and a reheated slice; a 9L oven fits a small baking tray. Think of the biggest thing you cook for yourself and check the interior dimensions in the listing rather than the slice rating.

Wattage tells you how quickly an oven reaches temperature. At 800W or 1800W, preheat is shorter than a typical budget oven. For a single meal that is a big part of the experience, since a ten-minute preheat for a five-minute reheat feels wasteful.

whatMatters.factor: Analog dials or a smart interface
whatMatters.detail: Dials are fast and need no learning. Smart ovens adjust power to the load. Pick dials if you cook simple things, and a smart oven if you want better results from small portions. Check that your chosen oven's controls match how you cook.

A toaster oven that does not fit under a cabinet becomes a nuisance. Measure the clear height and depth where you plan to put it, and add a couple of inches behind for ventilation. Look for the exterior dimensions in the spec table.
A 15-minute timer is fine for toast but short for roasting. A 30-minute timer lets you bake a small tray. If you want to cook real meals, check the maximum timer, not just whether a timer exists.

faq.q: What size toaster oven is best for one person?
faq.a: A compact oven around 9L, such as the Elite Gourmet ETO449X, fits a real single meal. A 2-slice model like the ETO236 only suits toast and reheating.

faq.q: Is a smart oven worth it for one person?
faq.a: If you cook proper meals often, yes. The Breville BOV450XL adjusts power for small loads. For toast and reheating a dial oven is enough.

faq.q: Can a toaster oven replace an air fryer?
faq.a: The Breville BOV680BSS has an air fry mode, so one appliance can do both. The other ovens here do not air fry.

faq.q: Will a toaster oven fit under a cabinet?
faq.a: Check the exterior height and add clearance for heat. The ETO236 and Dash Mini are the lowest-profile picks.

faq.q: How do I reheat leftovers without drying them out?
faq.a: Use a lower temperature with a loose foil cover, or a dedicated mode like Crispy Reheat on the Breville BOV680BSS.

faq.q: Is the Hamilton Beach 2-in-1 better than buying a separate toaster?
faq.a: If counter space is limited, yes. It combines the two. If you have room, a dedicated toaster plus a small oven may give more flexibility.

finalTake: For most single cooks, the Breville BOV450XL Mini Smart Oven is the right buy: sized for one and better at heating small portions. Choose the Breville BOV680BSS if you want air frying too. If the budget is tight, the Elite Gourmet ETO449X is the best simple oven, and the Dash Mini or ETO236 handle toast and reheating for little money.
